title: Why You Shouldn't Lay a Sanitary Tee on Its Side
description: Laying a standard sanitary tee horizontally to join a waste branch into a drain line is a frequent installation mistake. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal transitions, where gravity assists the directional change. When installed horizontally, the short-radius sweep fails to properly direct solid waste down the line, often leading to slow drainage, standing waste, and frequent clogs. Professional plumbers use combination wyes or long-turn sweeps for horizontal transitions to maintain proper flow velocity and prevent waste buildup. Always consult local plumbing codes for approved fitting orientations.

Why You Shouldn't Lay a Sanitary Tee on Its Side

Always consult local plumbing codes for approved fitting orientations.
